title: Optimize kernel selection and attention scheduling across H100/L40S/A10 with MIG partitions and GPU clock tuning
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Background: We need to reduce tail latency and improve throughput for long-context serving (prefill-heavy workloads) and mixed prefill/decode mixes across our supported hardware fleet (H100, L40S, A10). Prior work focused on algorithmic attention optimizations and kernel fusion; this ticket targets the hardware side: selecting the best kernel variants and scheduling prefill vs decode to specific MIG partitions, and tuning GPU clocks/power to find stable performance operating points.

Goals: 
- Identify per-device optimal kernel selection (tensor core vs non-tensor, fused attention kernels) across representative model sizes (1B, 7B, 13B) and sequence lengths (2k, 8k).
- Establish MIG partition configurations that maximize throughput per dollar for multi-tenant inference on H100/A10 nodes without regressing SLOs.
- Define prefill/decode scheduling policy that pins prefill-heavy requests to full instances and routes steady low-latency decode to MIG slices when beneficial.
- Find safe GPU clock/power configurations (using nvidia-smi -ac / vendor APIs) that improve determinism without thermal throttling in our cloud setup.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Median tail latency (p99) reduction >= 12% on 8k prefill workloads compared to baseline (runtime-1.20 kernels).
- Throughput (tokens/sec) improvement >= 1.15x for 13B models on H100 under 50% load.
- Cost-per-token improvement on multi-tenant MIG setups >= 8% vs baseline dedicated instances.

Approach / Plan: 
1) Benchmark matrix: H100 / L40S / A10 x model sizes x seq lengths x kernel variants x MIG partitions. Use existing perf harness (github link below) to produce stable curves.
2) Kernel probing: add telemetry hooks to runtime to report which kernel variant is selected and per-op timing to perf traces. Instrument attention kernel decision path to allow override for experiment runs.
3) MIG experiments: provision controlled nodes with 1g/2g/3g partitions (where supported) and run controlled multi-tenant mixes to measure throughput and latencies.
4) Clock tuning: run sustained load tests while sweeping GPU clocks (conservative -> recommended max) and monitor power, temperature, and perf. Identify operating points that avoid thermal throttling in our datacenter.
5) Scheduling policy: implement policy prototype in router layer to tag requests (prefill-heavy / decode-heavy / latency-sensitive) and test routing to instance types.

Artifacts / Links: 
- Perf harness (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pulls/412 (PR adding kernel-timing hooks)
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RT/pages/112233/Hardware+kernel+selection+and+MIG+policy
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt-hw/perf-hw-mig (live perf dashboards for experiments)

Risks / Trade-offs: 
- Aggressive clock overdrive yields better throughput but increases thermal events on our colocation hosts; we must balance improved perf with SLO stability.
- MIG configurations reduce per-instance peak performance; for models with very large KV state (long contexts) MIG slices may not be viable.
- Kernel selection complexity increases testing surface area; we will gate changes behind A/B rollouts and rollout policies.

Test plan: 
- Microbenchmarks: per-op timing for attention, matmul, softmax on single-GPU runs. Run each configuration 30 iterations to stabilize.
- End-to-end serving tests: run realistic request mixes from the harness (50/30/20 prefill/decode/short-chat) blast runs for 1 hour and measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
- Regression: for each candidate kernel/policy, run nightly regression suite across the fleet to guard against quality regressions.

Next steps: 
- Provision H100 and L40S nodes in PRD-like thermal profile (infra ticket INF-2543).
- Complete PR adding kernel-timing hooks and small opt-in knob for kernel override.
- Run first MIG sweep on A10 and H100 (1g/2g slices) this week and upload dashboards.

Notes: This ticket spans infra, runtime, and ops. Coordinate with infra for clock changes and with SRE for thermal monitoring.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Kernel timing instrumentation present and collected in perf harness for H100/L40S/A10.
2) MIG sweep completed with dashboards uploaded and documented conclusions.
3) Prototype router policy implemented and validated in staging with 10% traffic canary.
4) A recommended clock/power operating point documented and approved by SRE.
5) Measured improvements meet success criteria or ticket updated with mitigation plan.
updates: 2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with infra and SRE. Infra will provision H100 node with power telemetry; SRE asked for conservative clock limits during canary.

2026-03-05: Added kernel-timing hooks to perf harness (PR #412). Initial microbenchmarks show fused attention kernel is 9-11% faster on H100 for 2k context compared to baseline; improvements diminish at 8k due to memory-bound KV cache behavior.

2026-03-08: L40S single-GPU runs show good regressed performance for 7B with mixed-precision kernels; need to validate on multi-GPU pods with PCIe topology. Opened dependency ENG-7098 to provision 4xL40S test pod.

2026-03-11: First MIG partition runs on A10 (1g/2g) completed. Observed 18% lower cost-per-token on 1g when request size << model capacity, but p99 increases for long-context prefill workloads. Documented in dashboard and added to Confluence.

2026-03-13: Clock sweep on H100 showed best sustained throughput at recommended vendor clocks (-ac setting X), but thermal headroom is tight on certain hosts. SRE requested conservative canary for production. Planning a staged rollout behind runtime-1.21 canary gates.

2026-03-14: Implemented router tag 'prefill-heavy' and ran staging canary with 5% traffic. Initial results: p99 for prefill routed to full-instance improved by 14% while overall system cost drift was within expected bounds. Need to run 24h stability test before expanding canary.
